title.en: Volume 288 Biographies 47: Ren Zhongzheng, Zhou Qi, Cheng Lin, Jiang Zun, Fan Yong, Zhao Zhen, Ren Bu, Gao Ruone, Sun Mian
title.raw: 卷二百八十八 列傳第四十七 任中正 周起 程琳 姜遵 范雍 趙稹 任布 高若訥 孫沔 Volume 288 Biographies 47: Ren Zhongzheng, Zhou Qi, Cheng Lin, Jiang Zun, Fan Yong, Zhao Zhen, Ren Bu, Gao Ruone, Sun Mian

sentences.zh: 任中正

translations.literal: Ren Zhongzheng
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhongzheng

sentences.zh: 任中正，字慶之，曹州濟陰人。

translations.literal: Ren Zhongzheng, courtesy name Qingzhi, was a native of Jiyin in Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zhongzheng, styled Qingzhi, came from Jiyin in Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 父載，右拾遺。

translations.literal: His father Zai was a Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zai had served as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 中正進士及第，為池州推官。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng passed the jinshi examination and served as judicial assistant in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, Zhongzheng became judicial assistant at Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 歷大理評事、通判邵州，改太府寺丞、通判濮州。

translations.literal: He successively served as judicial reviewer in the Court of the Ministry of Justice, vice-prefect of Shaozhou, then as assistant director of the Court of Imperial Treasury and vice-prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Dali review officer and vice-prefect of Shaozhou, then became assistant director of the Court of Imperial Treasury and vice-prefect of Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士錢若水薦，遷秘書省著作佐郎、通判大名府。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Hanlin academician Qian Ruoshui, he was promoted to assistant compiler in the Secretariat and vice-prefect of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Hanlin academician Qian Ruoshui, he was made assistant compiler in the Secretariat and vice-prefect of Daming.

sentences.zh: 轉運使陳緯徙陝西，舉中正自代，太宗曰：「朕自知之。」

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Chen Wei was transferred to Shaanxi and recommended Zhongzheng to replace him. Emperor Taizong said, "I myself already know of him."
translations.idiomatic: When transport commissioner Chen Wei was posted to Shaanxi, he nominated Zhongzheng as his successor. Taizong replied, "I already have him in mind."

sentences.zh: 召為秘書丞、江南轉運副使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to serve as secretariat director and vice commissioner of the Jiangnan Transport Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng was summoned to be secretariat director and deputy transport commissioner for Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 中正軀幹頎長，帝擇大笏，命內臣取緋衣之長者賜之。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng was exceptionally tall in stature. The Emperor selected a large court tablet and ordered a eunuch to take the longest of the scarlet robes and grant it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng was unusually tall, so the Emperor chose an oversize court tablet and had a eunuch pick out the longest scarlet robe for him.

sentences.zh: 至部，歲大稔，民出租賦、平糴皆盈羨。

translations.literal: When he arrived at his post, the year's harvest was abundant, and the people's tax payments and government grain purchases both showed a surplus.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching his jurisdiction, harvests were abundant and both tax receipts and government grain purchases ran well above quota.

sentences.zh: 發運使王子輿欲悉調餉京師，中正曰：「東南歲輸五百餘萬，而江南所出過半。

translations.literal: Transport intendant Wang Ziyu wished to transfer all provisions to the capital. Zhongzheng said, "The southeast supplies more than five million each year, and Jiangnan contributes more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Transport intendant Wang Ziyu wanted to forward every surplus bushel to the capital. Zhongzheng objected: "The southeast sends more than five million shi yearly, and Jiangnan alone supplies over half.

sentences.zh: 今歲有餘，或歲少歉則數不登，患及吾民矣。」

translations.literal: This year there is a surplus, but if some year brings slight shortage the quotas will not be met, and the harm will fall on our people."
translations.idiomatic: We have a surplus now, but one lean year and quotas will fail—and our people will bear the cost."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wang desisted.

sentences.zh: 擢監察御史、兩浙轉運使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising censor and transport commissioner of the Two Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to supervising censor and transport commissioner for the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 民饑，中正不俟詔，發官廩振之。

translations.literal: When the people faced famine, Zhongzheng, without waiting for an edict, opened official granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, Zhongzheng opened government granaries to feed the people without waiting for orders.

sentences.zh: 按晉州盛梁獄，論如法。

translations.literal: He investigated the Sheng Liang case in Jin Prefecture and judged it according to law.
translations.idiomatic: He reviewed the Sheng Liang case in Jin Prefecture and ruled according to statute.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史、判三司憑由司。

translations.literal: He was transferred to palace attendant censor and assigned to the Three Departments Voucher Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made palace attendant censor and put in charge of the Three Departments Voucher Office.

sentences.zh: 既而有與梁善者，密中之，出為荊湖轉運使。

translations.literal: Afterwards someone friendly with Liang secretly slandered Zhongzheng, and he was sent out as transport commissioner of Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Later, an ally of Liang whispered against him, and Zhongzheng was posted out as transport commissioner for Jing and Hu.

sentences.zh: 遷左司諫、直史館、知梓州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left remonstrating censor, made a compiler at the Historiography Institute, and appointed prefect of Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He became left remonstrating censor, took up a post at the Historiography Institute, and was named prefect of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢樞密直學士，代張詠知益州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and replaced Zhang Yong as prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs, he succeeded Zhang Yong as prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡五載，遵詠條教，蜀人便之。

translations.literal: During five years in the prefecture, he followed Zhang Yong's regulations and policies, and the people of Shu found them convenient.
translations.idiomatic: For five years he kept Zhang Yong's rules in force, to the satisfaction of the Shu people.

sentences.zh: 知審刑院，出知幷州。

translations.literal: He served as head of the Court for Review of Penalties, then went out as prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After heading the Court for Review of Penalties, he was sent out as prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretariat drafter and given provisional charge of the Kaifeng Prefecture administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretariat drafter and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符九年，拜尚書工部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Works and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1016, he received appointment as vice minister of Works and vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 馬知節知密院，改同知院事。

translations.literal: When Ma Zhijie took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhongzheng's title was changed to co-administrator of the Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Zhijie headed the Bureau, Zhongzheng's role became co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，曹利用為樞密使，復為副使，再進兵部侍郎、參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year, when Cao Liyong became commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, Zhongzheng again served as vice commissioner and was further promoted to vice minister of War and participation in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, with Cao Liyong as commissioner, Zhongzheng returned as vice commissioner and was further promoted to vice minister of War and councilor.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮時，以右丞兼賓客。

translations.literal: When Renzong was crown prince, Zhongzheng served concurrently as Right Vice Director and attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong was crown prince, Zhongzheng served concurrently as right vice director and attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 帝既即位，乃拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: After the Emperor acceded, he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor acceded, he was appointed minister of War.

sentences.zh: 中正素與丁謂善，謂且貶，左右莫敢言者，中正獨營救謂，降太子賓客、知鄆州。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng had long been on good terms with Ding Wei. When Wei was about to be demoted, none among those around the throne dared speak for him, but Zhongzheng alone interceded. Zhongzheng was reduced to attendant of the crown prince and made prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng had long been friendly with Ding Wei. When Wei was about to be demoted, none at court dared speak for him, but Zhongzheng alone interceded and was himself reduced to crown prince attendant and made prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 中正弟尚書兵部員外郎、判三司鹽鐵勾院中行，右正言中師，皆坐貶。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng's younger brothers Zhongxing, vice director in the Ministry of War and controller of the Salt and Iron Commission's examination office, and Zhongshi, right remonstrator, were both implicated and demoted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng's younger brothers Zhongxing, vice director in the Ministry of War and controller of the Salt and Iron Commission's examination office, and Zhongshi, right remonstrator, were both implicated and demoted.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以母老徙曹州，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long, because his mother was old he was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, because his mother was old he was transferred to Caozhou and promoted to minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射，諡康懿。

translations.literal: He died. Posthumously he was granted Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He died. Posthumously he was granted left vice director of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Kangyi.

sentences.zh: 初，中正母入謁禁中，與陳彭年、王曾、張知白妻同見真宗，命中正母為班首，且賜坐。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongzheng's mother entered the inner palace for an audience. Together with the wives of Chen Pengnian, Wang Zeng, and Zhang Zhibai she was received by Emperor Zhenzong, who designated Zhongzheng's mother senior in rank among them and granted her a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhongzheng's mother entered the palace for an audience alongside the wives of Chen Pengnian, Wang Zeng, and Zhang Zhibai. Zhenzong seated her at the head of the group and gave her a chair.

sentences.zh: 中正事親孝，平居簡素，而飲食極豐美。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng was filial toward his parents; in daily life he was plain and frugal, yet his food and drink were extremely lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng was deeply filial, lived plainly on ordinary days, yet served his parents the finest food and wine.

sentences.zh: 弟 中師

translations.literal: Younger brother: Zhongshi
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Zhongshi

sentences.zh: 中師，字祖聖，進士及第，試秘書省校書郎、知平陸縣。

translations.literal: Zhongshi, courtesy name Zusheng, passed the jinshi examination and was tried out as proofreader in the Secretariat and appointed magistrate of Pinglu County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshi, styled Zusheng, passed the jinshi and, after a probationary stint as Secretariat proofreader, became magistrate of Pinglu County.

sentences.zh: 真宗將祀汾陰，命陳堯叟判河中府，以經制祀事，辟掌箋奏，累遷著作佐郎，歷知千乘、襄邑縣，改秘書丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong was about to sacrifice at Fenyin, he appointed Chen Yaosou to administer Hezhong Prefecture to oversee sacrificial affairs; Zhongshi was recruited to manage memorial drafts, was repeatedly promoted to assistant compiler, served successively as magistrate of Qiansheng and Xiangyi counties, and was changed to secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong prepared the Fenyin rites, Chen Yaosou was put in charge of Hezhong to manage the worship; Zhongshi joined his staff to draft memorials, rose to assistant compiler, served as magistrate of Qiansheng and Xiangyi, then became secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 以張知白薦，遂為右正言。

translations.literal: On Zhang Zhibai's recommendation, he became right remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhang Zhibai's recommendation, he was made right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 中正貶，中師亦降太常博士、監宿州酒稅。

translations.literal: When Zhongzheng was demoted, Zhongshi was also reduced to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and supervisor of Suzhou wine tax.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongzheng was demoted, Zhongshi was likewise reduced to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and put in charge of Suzhou's wine tax.

sentences.zh: 未幾，通判應天府。

translations.literal: Before long he served as vice-prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became vice-prefect of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 曹利用辟為群牧判官，徙知滑州，入為開封府判官。

translations.literal: Cao Liyong recruited him as judicial officer of the Pasturage Commission; he was transferred to serve as prefect of Huazhou, then entered the capital as judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Liyong brought him on as judicial officer of the Pasturage Commission; he was posted to Huazhou, then recalled to serve as judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書度支郎中、直史館、知澶州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director in the Ministry of Revenue's fiscal bureau, given a post at the Historiography Institute, and appointed prefect of Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Revenue's fiscal bureau, took a post at the Historiography Institute, and was named prefect of Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以太常少卿、直昭文館知廣州。

translations.literal: As vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler at the Hall of Spreading Culture, he was appointed prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to Guangzhou as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and compiler at the Hall of Spreading Culture.

sentences.zh: 視事之明日，吏白故事當謁諸祠廟，而廨有淫祠，中師遽命撤去之。

translations.literal: On the day after he assumed office, an official reported that by precedent he should visit the various temples, but the yamen contained illicit shrines, and Zhongshi immediately ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: The day after taking office, a clerk noted that custom required visits to local temples—but the yamen housed illicit shrines, which Zhongshi ordered torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 兼市舶使，市舶置使自此始。

translations.literal: He also served as maritime trade commissioner; the establishment of a maritime trade commissioner began from this.
translations.idiomatic: He also held the post of maritime trade commissioner—the first time that office was created.

sentences.zh: 還，為諫議大夫、判尚書刑部。

translations.literal: Upon returning, he served as remonstrating grandee and was assigned to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court, he became remonstrating grandee with charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 加集賢院學士，再知澶州。

translations.literal: He was additionally made academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and again appointed prefect of Chanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies and sent back to Chanzhou as prefect.

sentences.zh: 未行，進龍圖閣直學士、知幷州，許便宜從事。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was advanced to Hanlin academician at the Hall of Dragon Images and appointed prefect of Bingzhou, with permission to act at his discretion.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, he was promoted to Hanlin academician at the Hall of Dragon Images and named prefect of Bingzhou, with authority to act as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 改樞密直學士、知益州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，轉運使韓瀆急於籠利，自薪芻、蔬果之屬皆有算，而中師盡奏蠲之。

translations.literal: Earlier, transport commissioner Han Du had been eager to amass profit; even firewood, fodder, vegetables, and fruit were taxed, but Zhongshi memorialized to have all these remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, transport commissioner Han Du had taxed everything he could reach—even firewood, fodder, vegetables, and fruit—so Zhongshi memorialized to abolish the levies entirely.

sentences.zh: 康定中，任布守河陽，數上書論事，帝欲用之。

translations.literal: During the Kangding era, Ren Bu guarded Heyang and repeatedly submitted memorials discussing affairs of state; the Emperor wished to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: During Kangding, Ren Bu held Heyang and sent repeated memorials on state affairs; the Emperor meant to bring him into office.

sentences.zh: 呂夷簡薦中師才不在任布下，遂並召為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Lü Yijian recommended that Zhongshi's talent was not inferior to Ren Bu's, and both were summoned as vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yijian argued that Zhongshi was Ren Bu's equal in talent, and both men were summoned as vice commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，建北京，令中師領修建。

translations.literal: The next year, when the Northern Capital was established, Zhongshi was ordered to oversee its construction.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the Northern Capital was founded, Zhongshi was put in charge of building it.

sentences.zh: 進給事中，宣撫河東，不行。

translations.literal: He was promoted to supervising secretariat drafter and appointed pacification commissioner of Hedong, but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to supervising secretariat drafter, he was named pacification commissioner of Hedong but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 求補郡，以尚書禮部侍郎、資政殿學士知永興軍。

translations.literal: He requested a prefectural appointment and was made vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance, administering Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking a provincial post, he was made vice minister of Rites and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance, with charge of Yongxing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 求內徙，得知陳州。

translations.literal: He requested transfer inland and was appointed prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to be moved inland and was made prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾年，上書言：「臣老矣，家本曹人，願得守曹。」

translations.literal: After more than a year, he submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant is old; my family is originally from Caozhou, and I wish to be allowed to govern Caozhou."
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he wrote: "I am growing old, and my family roots lie in Caozhou—I would be grateful to serve there."

sentences.zh: 遂以知曹州。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed prefect of Caozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted, and he became prefect of Caozhou.

sentences.zh: 改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His title was changed to vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，請老，拜太子少傅致仕，進少師。

translations.literal: The next year he requested retirement on grounds of age, was appointed junior tutor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office, and was advanced to junior preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to retire; he was made junior tutor of the Heir Apparent, granted retirement, and advanced to junior preceptor.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太傅，諡安惠。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted senior tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made senior tutor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Anhui.

sentences.zh: 中師性樂易，平居自奉甚儉約，晚知養生之術，號「大塊翁」。

translations.literal: Zhongshi was easygoing by nature; in daily life he was very frugal in his personal upkeep, and in later years, having learned the arts of nurturing life, he styled himself "Old Man of the Great Clod."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshi was good-natured and lived simply for himself; in his later years he studied the arts of longevity and took the sobriquet "Old Man of the Great Clod."

sentences.zh: 周起，字萬卿，淄州鄒平人。

translations.literal: Zhou Qi, courtesy name Wanqing, was a native of Zouping in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Qi, styled Wanqing, came from Zouping in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 生而豐下，父意異之，曰：「此兒必起吾門。」

translations.literal: At birth he had a broad lower face; his father thought him unusual and said, "This child will surely raise our house."
translations.idiomatic: He was born with a broad lower face; his father took this as a sign and said, "This boy will lift our house."

sentences.zh: 因名起。

translations.literal: Therefore he was named Qi.
translations.idiomatic: So he was given the name Qi.

sentences.zh: 幼敏慧如成人。

translations.literal: As a child he was clever and perceptive like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he was as sharp as a grown man.

sentences.zh: 意知衛州，坐事削官，起才十三，詣京師訟父冤，父乃得復故官。

translations.literal: His father Yi served as prefect of Weizhou and was stripped of office for an offense; Qi was only thirteen, yet went to the capital to plead his father's innocence, and his father was thereby restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yi was prefect of Weizhou until an offense cost him his rank; Qi was only thirteen when he went to the capital to plead his father's case and won his reinstatement.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，授將作監丞、通判齊州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi, he was made director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings and vice-prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢著作佐郎、直史館，累遷戶部、度支判官。

translations.literal: He was promoted to assistant compiler and given a post at the Historiography Institute, and was repeatedly transferred to serve as judicial officer in the Ministry of Revenue and its fiscal bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to assistant compiler with a post at the Historiography Institute, then served successively as judicial officer in the Ministry of Revenue and its fiscal bureau.

sentences.zh: 真宗北征，領隨軍糧草事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhenzong marched north, Qi took charge of the army's grain and fodder.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhenzong's northern campaign, Qi managed the army's grain and fodder supply.

sentences.zh: 以右正言知制誥，權判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: As right remonstrator he was entrusted with drafting edicts and given provisional charge of the Ministry of Personnel's within-the-passes selection board.
translations.idiomatic: As right remonstrator he drafted edicts and was given provisional charge of the Ministry of Personnel's within-the-passes selection board.

sentences.zh: 尋為東京留守判官，判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he served as judicial officer to the Eastern Capital garrison commander and was assigned to the Drum and Appeal Court.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became judicial officer to the Eastern Capital garrison commander and took charge of the Drum and Appeal Court.

sentences.zh: 封泰山，攝御史中丞、考制度副使，所過得采訪官吏能否及民利病以聞。

translations.literal: During the Mount Tai feng sacrifice, he acted as vice censor-in-chief and deputy commissioner for examining institutions; wherever he passed he was permitted to investigate officials' competence and the people's hardships and report them.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mount Tai feng rite he served as acting vice censor-in-chief and deputy commissioner for examining institutions, with authority to report on officials' competence and the people's hardships wherever he traveled.

sentences.zh: 東封還，近臣率頌功德，起獨以居安為戒。

translations.literal: After returning from the eastern feng, close ministers all praised the emperor's merit and virtue; Qi alone warned against complacency in peace.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern feng, court favorites all praised the emperor's achievements; Qi alone cautioned against resting easy in peace.

sentences.zh: 進金部員外郎、判集賢院。

translations.literal: He was promoted to outer-section director in the Ministry of Revenue's treasury bureau and assigned to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He was made outer-section director in the Ministry of Revenue's treasury bureau and put in charge of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 初置糾察刑獄司，因命起，起乃請諸已決而事有所枉及官吏非理榜掠者，並聽受訴，從之。

translations.literal: When the Office for Investigating Penal Affairs was first established, Qi was appointed to it; he then requested that all cases already decided in which there had been injustice, as well as cases of officials' unlawful beating and flogging, be allowed to receive appeals, and this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the Office for Investigating Penal Affairs was first created, Qi was put in charge; he asked that closed cases involving injustice and unlawful beatings by officials be opened to appeal, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 擢樞密直學士、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and given provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and made acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 起聽斷明審，舉無留事。

translations.literal: Qi heard cases with clarity and precision, and nothing was left pending.
translations.idiomatic: Qi judged cases with clarity and left no backlog.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘗臨幸問勞，起請曰：「陛下昔龍潛於此，請避正寢，居西廡。」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong once visited in person to inquire after him; Qi requested, "Your Majesty once lived here before ascending the throne—please avoid the main chamber and stay in the west wing."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong visited in person, Qi asked: "Your Majesty once lived here before taking the throne—please leave the main chamber and stay in the west wing."

sentences.zh: 詔從之，名其堂曰「繼照」。

translations.literal: An edict approved this, and the hall was named "Continuing Radiance."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, and the hall was named "Continuing Radiance."

sentences.zh: 起嘗奏事殿中，適仁宗始生，帝曰：「卿知朕喜乎？

translations.literal: Once when Qi was reporting in the hall, Renzong had just been born. The Emperor said, "Do you know why I am pleased?
translations.idiomatic: Once while Qi was reporting in court, Renzong had just been born. The emperor said, "Do you know why I am happy?

sentences.zh: 宜賀我有子矣」即入禁中，懷金錢出，探以賜起。

translations.literal: You should congratulate me—I have a son." He immediately entered the inner palace, came out with gold coins in his sleeve, and drew them out to grant to Qi."
translations.idiomatic: You should congratulate me—I have a son." He went into the inner palace, returned with gold coins in his sleeve, and pressed them into Qi's hand."

sentences.zh: 改勾當三班院兼判登聞檢院。

translations.literal: He was changed to administrator of the Three-Rank Office and concurrently assigned to the Petition Review Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was made administrator of the Three-Rank Office and also put in charge of the Petition Review Court.

sentences.zh: 從祀汾陰，貿權知河中府，徙永興、天雄軍，所至有風烈，數賜書褒諭。

translations.literal: After accompanying the Fenyin sacrifice, he was given provisional charge of Hezhong Prefecture, was transferred to Yongxing and Tianxiong Circuit, and wherever he went he showed force of character; the emperor repeatedly sent letters of praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: After the Fenyin rites he was given provisional charge of Hezhong, then posted to Yongxing and Tianxiong Circuit; wherever he served he made a strong impression, and the emperor repeatedly sent letters of praise.

sentences.zh: 三遷右諫議大夫、知幷州。

translations.literal: After three promotions he became right remonstrating grandee and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he was made right remonstrating grandee and prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 拜給事中、同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed supervising secretariat drafter and co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretariat drafter and co-administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 進禮部侍郎，為樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and served as vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of Rites and made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 嘗與寇準過同列曹瑋家飲酒，既而客多引去者，獨起與寇準盡醉，夜漏上乃歸。

translations.literal: Once he and Kou Zhun stopped by the home of their colleague Cao Wei for wine; afterward most guests withdrew, but Qi alone drank with Kou Zhun until thoroughly drunk, and only returned after the night watch had sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Once he and Kou Zhun drank at colleague Cao Wei's home; when most guests left, he and Kou Zhun drank on until midnight.

sentences.zh: 明日入見，引咎伏謝。

translations.literal: The next day he entered audience, accepted blame, and prostrated himself in apology.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he appeared at court, accepted blame, and apologized.

sentences.zh: 真宗笑曰：「天下無事，大臣相與飲酒，何過之有？」

translations.literal: Emperor Zhenzong laughed and said, "The realm is at peace—what fault is there in great ministers drinking together?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong laughed: "The realm is at peace—what fault is there in ministers drinking together?"

sentences.zh: 起素善寇準。

translations.literal: Qi had long been on good terms with Kou Zhun.
translations.idiomatic: Qi had long been close to Kou Zhun.

sentences.zh: 準且貶，起亦罷為戶部郎中、知青州，又降太常少卿、知光州。

translations.literal: When Kou Zhun was about to be demoted, Qi was also dismissed and made director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of Qingzhou, then further reduced to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun was demoted, Qi was removed from office and made director in the Ministry of Revenue and prefect of Qingzhou, then further reduced to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷秘書監，徙揚、杭二州，又徙應天府。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to director of the Secretariat and transferred to Yangzhou and Hangzhou, then again to Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to director of the Secretariat, served in Yangzhou and Hangzhou, then was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 復為禮部侍郎、判登聞鼓院。

translations.literal: He again served as vice minister of the Ministry of Rites and was assigned to the Drum and Appeal Court.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice minister of Rites and put in charge of the Drum and Appeal Court.

sentences.zh: 以疾請知潁州，徙陳州、汝州。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested appointment as prefect of Yingzhou and was transferred to Chenzhou and Ruzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he asked to be prefect of Yingzhou and was later moved to Chenzhou and Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈禮部尚書，諡安惠。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted minister of the Ministry of Rites and given the posthumous title Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Anhui.

sentences.zh: 起性周密，凡奏事及答禁中語，隨輒焚草，故其言，外人無知者。

translations.literal: Qi was meticulous by nature; whenever he reported on affairs or answered words from within the palace, he immediately burned his drafts, so outsiders knew nothing of what he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was meticulous by nature; after every report or reply to palace business he burned his drafts, so outsiders never learned what he had said.

sentences.zh: 家藏書至萬餘卷。

translations.literal: His household collection of books reached more than ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His family library held more than ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 起能書。

translations.literal: Qi was skilled at calligraphy.
translations.idiomatic: Qi was an accomplished calligrapher.

sentences.zh: 弟超，亦能書，集古今人書並所更體法，為《書苑》十卷，累官主客郎中。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chao was also skilled at calligraphy; he collected ancient and modern calligraphy together with styles he had revised and compiled them into ten scrolls titled 《Garden of Calligraphy》, and rose through the ranks to director in the Ministry of Rites' guest bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Chao was also a calligrapher; he compiled ancient and modern scripts together with revised styles into the ten-scroll 《Garden of Calligraphy》 and rose to director in the Ministry of Rites' guest bureau.

sentences.zh: 起子：延荷，以孝友聞，官殿中丞；

translations.literal: Qi's sons: Yanhe, known for filial piety and brotherly affection, served as palace censor;
translations.idiomatic: Qi's sons: Yanhe, famed for filial piety and brotherly devotion, served as palace censor;

sentences.zh: 延雋，頗雅厚，官太常少卿。

translations.literal: Yanjuan, quite refined and generous, served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjuan, refined and generous in manner, served as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 程琳，字天球，永寧軍博野人。

translations.literal: Cheng Lin, courtesy name Tianqiu, was a native of Boye in Yongning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lin, styled Tianqiu, came from Boye in Yongning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 舉服勤辭學科，補泰寧軍節度推官。

translations.literal: He passed the examination in diligent service and literary composition and was appointed judicial assistant in the Taining Circuit military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination in diligent service and literary composition and became judicial assistant on the Taining Circuit military staff.

sentences.zh: 改秘書省著作佐郎、知壽陽縣，監左藏庫，召試，直集賢院。

translations.literal: He was changed to assistant compiler in the Secretariat and magistrate of Shouyang County, supervised the Left Storehouse, was summoned for examination, and was given a post at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He became assistant compiler in the Secretariat and magistrate of Shouyang County, supervised the Left Storehouse, passed a court examination, and was given a post at the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 改太常博士、權三司戶部判官，契丹館伴使。

translations.literal: He was changed to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and provisional judicial officer in the Three Departments' revenue bureau, and served as Khitan escort commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and provisional judicial officer in the Three Departments' revenue bureau, and served as escort commissioner for Khitan envoys.

sentences.zh: 契丹使者謂琳曰：「先皇帝嘗通使承天，太后獨無使，何也？」

translations.literal: A Khitan envoy said to Lin, "The late emperor once exchanged envoys with Chengtian, yet the empress dowager alone has no envoy—why?"
translations.idiomatic: A Khitan envoy asked Lin, "Your late emperor exchanged envoys with Chengtian, but the empress dowager sends none—why?"

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「南北，兄弟也。

translations.literal: Lin said, "North and south are brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied, "North and south are brothers.

sentences.zh: 先皇帝視承天猶從母，故無嫌；

translations.literal: The late emperor regarded Chengtian as a father's younger brother's wife, so there was no impropriety;
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor treated Chengtian as a father's younger brother's wife, so no impropriety was involved;

sentences.zh: 今皇太后乃嫂也，禮不通問。」

translations.literal: the present empress dowager is an elder brother's wife, and by ritual no communication is permitted."
translations.idiomatic: but the present empress dowager is an elder brother's wife, and ritual forbids such exchanges."

sentences.zh: 契丹使者語屈。

translations.literal: The Khitan envoy was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan envoy had no reply.

sentences.zh: 後修《真宗實錄》，而大中祥符以來起居注闕，琳追述上之，遂修起居注，提舉在京諸司庫務，知制誥、判吏部流內銓。

translations.literal: Later, when the Veritable Records of Zhenzong were compiled and the daily records from Dazhong Xiangfu onward were missing, Lin reconstructed and submitted them; he then compiled the daily records, supervised the storehouses of the capital offices, was entrusted with drafting edicts, and was assigned to the Ministry of Personnel's within-the-passes selection board.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Zhenzong were compiled and daily records from Dazhong Xiangfu onward were missing, Lin reconstructed and submitted them, then took charge of the daily records, supervised capital storehouses, drafted edicts, and ran the Ministry of Personnel's within-the-passes selection board.

sentences.zh: 權三司使范雍使契丹，命琳發遣三司使。

translations.literal: Acting Three Departments commissioner Fan Yong was sent as envoy to the Khitan; Lin was ordered to dispatch the Three Departments commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When acting Three Departments commissioner Fan Yong went as envoy to the Khitan, Lin was ordered to dispatch the Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 太倉贍軍粟陳腐不可食，歲且饑，琳盡發以貸民，凡六十萬斛，饑民賴以全活，而軍得善粟。

translations.literal: The grain in the Grand Storehouse for provisioning the army had gone stale and was inedible; famine was approaching, and Lin released all of it on loan to the people—six hundred thousand hu in all—so that starving people were preserved alive, while the army received good grain.
translations.idiomatic: Army grain in the Grand Storehouse had gone stale and was inedible; famine was near, so Lin released all of it on loan to the people—six hundred thousand hu in all—saving countless lives while the army received fresh grain.

sentences.zh: 鹽鐵官任布請鑄大錢一當十，度支判官許申請以銅鐵雜鑄，下其議。

translations.literal: Salt and iron official Ren Bu requested casting large coins worth ten each; fiscal bureau judicial officer Xu Shen requested mixed copper and iron casting, and the proposal was referred for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Salt and iron official Ren Bu proposed casting large coins worth ten each; fiscal bureau judicial officer Xu Shen proposed mixed copper and iron casting, and the matter was referred for discussion.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「第五琦用大錢，法卒不可行。

translations.literal: Lin said, "When Diwu Qi used large coins, the policy ultimately could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "When Diwu Qi used large coins, the policy ultimately failed.

sentences.zh: 乞令申試之。」

translations.literal: I request that Shen be allowed to try it."
translations.idiomatic: Let Shen try it, I ask."

sentences.zh: 鑄卒不就。

translations.literal: The casting ultimately failed.
translations.idiomatic: The casting never succeeded.

sentences.zh: 契丹遣蕭蘊、杜防來，蘊出位圖示琳曰：「中國使者坐殿上高位，今我位乃下，請升之。」

translations.literal: The Khitan sent Xiao Yun and Du Fang; Yun produced a seating chart and showed Lin, saying, "Song envoys sit in the high seats in the hall, yet our seats are lower—please raise them."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan sent Xiao Yun and Du Fang; Yun produced a seating chart and said to Lin, "Song envoys sit in the high seats in the hall, yet ours are lower—please raise them."

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「此真宗所定，不可易。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "This was fixed by Emperor Zhenzong and cannot be changed."
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied, "Emperor Zhenzong fixed this arrangement—it cannot be changed."

sentences.zh: 防曰：「“國之卿，可以當小國之君。」

translations.literal: Fang said, "A minister of a state may stand in for the ruler of a small state."
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "A minister of a great state may stand in for the ruler of a lesser one."

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「南北雖兩朝，無小大之異，卿嘗坐我殿上，我顧小國耶？」

translations.literal: Lin said, "North and south are two courts, but there is no difference of great and small—you once sat in our hall; do you take us for a small state?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "North and south are two courts, but not great and small—you once sat in our hall; do you take us for a lesser state?"

sentences.zh: 防無以對。

translations.literal: Fang had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fang had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 宰相將許之，琳曰：「許其小必啟其大。」

translations.literal: The chief ministers were about to agree; Lin said, "Granting a small concession will surely invite a larger one."
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers were about to agree; Lin warned, "Concede a small point and a larger demand will follow."

sentences.zh: 以右諫議大夫權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed right remonstrating grandee and acting vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made right remonstrating grandee and acting vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 宰相張知白尤器之，當除命，喜曰：「不辱吾筆矣。」

translations.literal: Chief minister Zhang Zhibai especially valued him; when the appointment was issued, he said with pleasure, "My recommendation has not been disgraced."
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Zhang Zhibai especially valued him; when the appointment came through, he said with satisfaction, "My recommendation has not been disgraced."

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，上疏請罷諸土木營造，蠲被災郡縣租賦。

translations.literal: Famine prevailed that year; he submitted a memorial requesting suspension of all construction projects and remission of taxes in disaster-stricken prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Famine prevailed that year; he memorialized to halt all construction and remit taxes in disaster-stricken prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 改樞密直學士、知益州。

translations.literal: He was changed to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and appointed prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin academician at the Bureau of Military Affairs and made prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 上元張燈，州人夜聚遊嬉，琳戒曰：「有火則隨救之，毋白也。」

translations.literal: On the Lantern Festival lanterns were hung; the people of the prefecture gathered at night to revel. Lin warned, "If fire breaks out, put it out at once—do not report it."
translations.idiomatic: On the Lantern Festival the prefecture hung lanterns and people gathered to celebrate at night. Lin warned, "If fire breaks out, put it out at once—do not report it."

sentences.zh: 已而果有火，終宴人無知者。

translations.literal: Fire did break out, yet by the end of the festivities no one knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: Fire did break out, yet by the end of the festivities no one had noticed.

sentences.zh: 或告振武軍變，琳曰：「軍中動靜我自知之，苟有謀，不待告也。」

translations.literal: Someone reported a mutiny at Zhenwu Army; Lin said, "I know the movements in the army myself—if there were a plot, I would not need to be told."
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported a mutiny at Zhenwu Army; Lin said, "I know what happens in the army—if there were a plot, I would not need to be told."

sentences.zh: 遷給事中、權知開封府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to supervising secretariat drafter and given provisional charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made supervising secretariat drafter and acting prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 王蒙正子齊雄捶老卒死，貸妻子使以病告。

translations.literal: Wang Mengzheng's son Qixiong beat an old soldier to death and lent money to the man's wife and children to report death by illness.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mengzheng's son Qixiong beat an old soldier to death and paid the man's wife and children to report death by illness.

sentences.zh: 琳察其色辭異，令有司驗得捶死狀。

translations.literal: Lin noticed their color and words were strange and ordered the authorities to examine the body, confirming death by beating.
translations.idiomatic: Lin noticed something odd in their manner and words and ordered an examination, which confirmed death by beating.

sentences.zh: 蒙正連姻章獻太后家，太后謂琳曰：「齊雄非殺人者，乃其奴嘗捶之。」

translations.literal: Mengzheng was related by marriage to Empress Dowager Zhangxian's family; the empress dowager told Lin, "Qixiong is not the killer—it was his servant who once beat the man."
translations.idiomatic: Mengzheng was related by marriage to Empress Dowager Zhangxian's family; the empress dowager told Lin, "Qixiong did not kill him—it was his servant who once beat the man."

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「奴無自專理，且使令與己犯同。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "A servant has no authority to act on his own, and moreover one who gives orders shares the same offense as the one who commits it."
translations.idiomatic: Lin replied, "A servant has no authority to act on his own, and one who gives orders shares the same offense as the one who commits it."

sentences.zh: 太后嘿然，遂論如法。

translations.literal: The empress dowager fell silent, and the case was judged according to law.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fell silent, and the case was judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 外戚吳氏離其夫而挈其女歸，夫訴於府。

translations.literal: A consort-clan woman surnamed Wu left her husband and took her daughter home; the husband appealed to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A consort-clan woman surnamed Wu left her husband and took their daughter home; the husband appealed to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琳命還女，吳氏曰：「已納宮中矣。」

translations.literal: Lin ordered the daughter returned; Wu said, "She has already been taken into the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Lin ordered the daughter returned; Wu said, "She has already been taken into the palace."

sentences.zh: 琳請於帝曰：「臣恐天下人有竊議陛下奪人妻女者。」

translations.literal: Lin appealed to the emperor, saying, "Your servant fears people throughout the realm will whisper that Your Majesty seized another man's wife and daughter."
translations.idiomatic: Lin appealed to the emperor: "I fear people throughout the realm will whisper that Your Majesty seized another man's wife and daughter."

sentences.zh: 帝亟命出之。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered her released.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered her released.

sentences.zh: 笞而歸其妻。

translations.literal: Wu was flogged and the wife was returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wu was flogged and the wife was returned to her husband.

sentences.zh: 遷工部侍郎、龍圖閣學士，復為御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Works and academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, and again served as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was made vice minister of Works and academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, and again served as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 不拜，以翰林侍讀學士兼龍圖閣學士再知開封府。

translations.literal: He did not accept the appointment and instead, as Hanlin reader-in-waiting and academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, again took charge of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the post and instead, as Hanlin reader-in-waiting and academician of the Hall of Dragon Images, again served as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 改三司使，出納尤謹，禁中有所取，輒奏罷之。

translations.literal: He was changed to Three Departments commissioner and was especially strict in receipts and disbursements; whenever the inner palace requested funds, he memorialized to halt it.
translations.idiomatic: He became Three Departments commissioner and was especially strict with receipts and disbursements; whenever the inner palace requested funds, he memorialized to block it.

sentences.zh: 內侍言琳專，琳曰：「三司財賦，皆朝廷有也。

translations.literal: A eunuch said Lin was overbearing; Lin said, "The Three Departments' revenues all belong to the court.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch accused Lin of being overbearing; Lin replied, "The Three Departments' revenues all belong to the court.

sentences.zh: 臣為陛下惜，於臣何有？」

translations.literal: Your servant is sparing them for Your Majesty—what does it have to do with me?"
translations.idiomatic: I am sparing them for Your Majesty—what does that have to do with me?"

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 或請併天下農田稅物名者，琳曰：「合而為一，易於勾校，可也。

translations.literal: Someone requested merging the names of all farmland tax items nationwide; Lin said, "Combining them into one would make auditing easier—that is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Someone proposed merging all farmland tax items nationwide; Lin said, "Combining them into one would make auditing easier—that is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 後有興利之臣，復用舊名增之，是重困民，無已時也。」

translations.literal: But later profit-seeking officials would revive the old names and add to them—this would doubly burden the people without end."
translations.idiomatic: But later profit-seeking officials would revive the old names and add to them—doubly burdening the people without end."

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部侍郎，遂參知政事，遷尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then became participation in state affairs, and was advanced to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made vice minister of Personnel, then became councilor, and was advanced to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 時元昊反，猶遣使來朝，眾請按誅之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuanhao had rebelled, yet still sent envoys to court; many requested that they be arrested and executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao had rebelled, yet still sent envoys to court; many demanded their arrest and execution.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「遣使，常事也，殺之不祥。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "Sending envoys is a routine matter; killing them is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Sending envoys is routine; killing them is inauspicious."

sentences.zh: 後使者益驕橫，大臣患之。

translations.literal: Later the envoys grew ever more arrogant and overbearing, and the great ministers were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Later the envoys grew ever more arrogant, and the great ministers were troubled.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「始不殺，無罪也；

translations.literal: Lin said, "At first we did not kill them—they were not guilty;
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "At first we did not kill them—they were not guilty;

sentences.zh: 今既驕橫，可暴其惡誅之，國法也，又何患耶？」

translations.literal: now that they are arrogant and overbearing, we may expose their wickedness and execute them—that is state law; what is there to worry about?"
translations.idiomatic: now that they are arrogant, we may expose their wickedness and execute them—that is state law; what is there to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 又議重賄唃廝囉使討賊，得地即與之。

translations.literal: Others also debated bribing Gusiluo heavily to attack the rebels and granting him any territory he captured.
translations.idiomatic: Others also debated bribing Gusiluo heavily to attack the rebels and granting him any territory he captured.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「使唃廝囉得地是復生一元昊矣。

translations.literal: Lin said, "If Gusiluo gains territory, that would be giving birth to another Yuanhao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "If Gusiluo gains territory, we would be creating another Yuanhao.

sentences.zh: 不若用間，使二羌勢不合，中國利也。」

translations.literal: Better to use stratagem and keep the two Qiang factions from uniting—that would benefit the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Better to use stratagem and keep the two Qiang factions from uniting—that would benefit the Middle Kingdom."

sentences.zh: 故樞密副使張遜第在武成坊，其曾孫偕才七歲，宗室女生也，貧不自給。

translations.literal: The former vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Zhang Xun's residence was in Wucheng Ward; his great-great-grandson Xie was only seven years old, born of an imperial clanswoman, and too poor to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Former vice commissioner Zhang Xun's residence stood in Wucheng Ward; his great-great-grandson Xie was only seven, born of an imperial clanswoman, and too poor to support himself.

sentences.zh: 乳媼擅出券鬻第，琳欲得之，使開封府吏密諭媼，以偕幼，宜得御寶許鬻乃售。

translations.literal: The wet nurse privately issued a deed and sold the residence; Lin wished to acquire it and had a Kaifeng Prefecture clerk secretly instruct the nurse that because Xie was young, an imperial seal permitting the sale should be obtained before it could be sold.
translations.idiomatic: The wet nurse privately issued a deed and sold the residence; Lin wanted it and had a Kaifeng clerk secretly tell the nurse that because Xie was young, an imperial seal permitting the sale was required.

sentences.zh: 乳媼以宗室女故，入宮見章惠太后。

translations.literal: Because the child was born of an imperial clanswoman, the wet nurse entered the palace to see Empress Dowager Zhanghui.
translations.idiomatic: Because the child was born of an imperial clanswoman, the wet nurse entered the palace to see Empress Dowager Zhanghui.

sentences.zh: 既得御寶，琳乃市取之。

translations.literal: Once the imperial seal was obtained, Lin then purchased it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial seal was obtained, Lin purchased the residence.

sentences.zh: 又令吏市材木，買婦女。

translations.literal: He also had clerks purchase timber and buy women.
translations.idiomatic: He also had clerks purchase timber and buy women.

sentences.zh: 已而吏以贓敗，御史按劾得狀，降光祿卿、知潁州。

translations.literal: Before long the clerk was exposed for corruption; the censorate investigated and confirmed the facts, and Lin was demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and appointed prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the clerk was exposed for corruption; the censorate investigated and confirmed the facts, and Lin was demoted to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and made prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為戶部侍郎，尋復吏部、知天雄軍。

translations.literal: Before long he served as vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, and soon again as vice minister of Personnel and administrator of Tianxiong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was vice minister of Revenue, then again vice minister of Personnel and administrator of Tianxiong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 又以左丞為資政殿學士。

translations.literal: He was also made left vice director and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made left vice director and academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance.

sentences.zh: 及建天雄軍為北京，內侍皇甫繼明主營宮室，欲侈大以要賞。

translations.literal: When Tianxiong Circuit was established as the Northern Capital, eunuch Huangfu Jiming supervised construction of the palace buildings and wished to make them extravagant and grand to win rewards.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxiong Circuit was established as the Northern Capital, eunuch Huangfu Jiming supervised palace construction and wished to make it extravagant to win rewards.

sentences.zh: 琳以為方事邊陲，又事土木以困民，不可。

translations.literal: Lin held that with border affairs pressing, undertaking construction to burden the people was unacceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Lin held that with border affairs pressing, undertaking construction to burden the people was unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 既而繼明數有論奏，帝遣御史魚周詢按視，遂罷繼明，命琳獨主之。

translations.literal: Before long Jiming repeatedly submitted memorials; the emperor sent censor Yu Zhouxun to inspect, then dismissed Jiming and ordered Lin alone to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jiming repeatedly submitted memorials; the emperor sent censor Yu Zhouxun to inspect, dismissed Jiming, and put Lin alone in charge.

sentences.zh: 遷工部尚書，加大學士、河北安撫使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Works, was additionally made grand academician, and appointed pacification commissioner of Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of Works, additionally grand academician, and pacification commissioner of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 改武昌軍節度使、知永興軍、陝西安撫使。

translations.literal: He was changed to military commissioner of Wuchang Circuit, administrator of Yongxing Circuit, and pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He became military commissioner of Wuchang Circuit, administrator of Yongxing Circuit, and pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽北院使判延州，仍為陝西安撫使。

translations.literal: As commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat he administered Yanzhou and continued as pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: As commissioner of the Northern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat he administered Yanzhou and continued as pacification commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 元昊死，諒祚立，方幼，三大將分治其國。

translations.literal: Yuanhao died and Liangzuo succeeded him while still young; three great generals divided rule of the state among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao died and Liangzuo succeeded him while still young; three great generals divided rule of the state among themselves.

sentences.zh: 議者謂可因此時，以節度使啖三將，使各有所部分，以弱其勢，可不戰而屈矣。

translations.literal: Advisors said that at this moment military commissioner titles could be used to entice the three generals, giving each his own portion and weakening their power, so that they could be subdued without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Advisors said that at this moment military commissioner titles could be used to entice the three generals, giving each his own portion and weakening their power, so that they could be subdued without fighting.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「幸人之喪，非所以柔遠人，不如因而撫之。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "Taking advantage of another's bereavement is not the way to soothe distant peoples; better to seize the occasion to reassure them."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Taking advantage of another's bereavement is not the way to soothe distant peoples; better to seize the occasion to reassure them."

sentences.zh: 議者惜其失機。

translations.literal: The advisors regretted the missed opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: The advisors regretted the missed opportunity.

sentences.zh: 既而遣使冊命，夏人方圍慶陽。

translations.literal: Before long envoys were sent to invest the new ruler; the Xia people were then besieging Qingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long envoys were sent to invest the new ruler while the Xia were besieging Qingyang.

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「彼若貪此，可緩慶州之難矣。」

translations.literal: Lin said, "If they covet this, the crisis at Qingzhou can be eased."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "If they covet this, the crisis at Qingzhou can be eased."

sentences.zh: 具禮幣賜予之數移報之，果喜，即日迎冊使，慶陽之圍亦解。

translations.literal: He prepared the full tally of ritual gifts and gifts to be bestowed and sent word; they were indeed pleased, welcomed the investiture envoys that very day, and the siege of Qingyang was also lifted.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared the full tally of ritual gifts and sent word; they were pleased, welcomed the investiture envoys that very day, and the siege of Qingyang was lifted.

sentences.zh: 嘗獲戎首，不殺，戒遣之，夏人亦相告毋捕漢民。

translations.literal: Once he captured a Rong chieftain but did not kill him, admonished him, and sent him back; the Xia people also told one another not to capture Han civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Once he captured a Rong chieftain but did not kill him, admonished him, and sent him back; the Xia also told one another not to capture Han civilians.

sentences.zh: 久之，以五百戶驅牛羊扣邊請降，且言：「契丹兵至衙頭矣，國中亂，願自歸。」

translations.literal: After some time, five hundred households drove cattle and sheep to the border to request surrender, saying, "Khitan troops have reached Yatou; the state is in turmoil, and we wish to submit ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: After some time, five hundred households drove cattle and sheep to the border to request surrender, saying, "Khitan troops have reached Yatou; the state is in turmoil, and we wish to submit."

sentences.zh: 琳曰：「彼詐也。

translations.literal: Lin said, "This is a ruse.
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "This is a ruse.

sentences.zh: 契丹至帳下，當舉國取之，豈容有來降者？

translations.literal: When the Khitan reach the royal tent, the whole state should be taken—how could there be people coming to surrender?
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan reach the royal tent, the whole state should be taken—how could there be people coming to surrender?

sentences.zh: 間聞夏人方捕叛者，此其是邪？

translations.literal: I have heard the Xia are hunting rebels—is this them?
translations.idiomatic: I have heard the Xia are hunting rebels—is this them?

sentences.zh: 不然，誘我也。」

translations.literal: If not, they are luring us."
translations.idiomatic: If not, they are luring us."

sentences.zh: 拒不受。

translations.literal: He refused to accept them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to accept them.

sentences.zh: 已而賊果以騎三萬臨境上，以捕降者為辭。

translations.literal: Before long the enemy indeed came with thirty thousand cavalry to the border, using the pursuit of deserters as their pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy came with thirty thousand cavalry to the border, using the pursuit of deserters as their pretext.

sentences.zh: 琳諜知之，閉壁倒旗，戒諸將勿動，賊疑有備，遂引去。

translations.literal: Lin learned this through spies, closed the walls, lowered the flags, and warned the generals not to move; the enemy suspected preparations and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Lin learned this through spies, closed the walls, lowered the flags, and warned the generals not to move; the enemy suspected preparations and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 拜同中書門下平章事、判大名府。

translations.literal: He was appointed co-director of the Department of State Affairs and given charge of Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed co-director of the Department of State Affairs and given charge of Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 琳持重不擾，前後守魏十年，度要害，繕壁壘，增守禦備。

translations.literal: Lin was steady and did not disturb the people; over ten years guarding Wei in succession, he assessed strategic points, repaired walls and ramparts, and increased defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was steady and did not disturb the people; over ten years guarding Wei, he assessed strategic points, repaired walls and ramparts, and strengthened defenses.

sentences.zh: 植雜木數萬，曰：「異時樓櫓之具，可不出於民矣。」

translations.literal: He planted tens of thousands of mixed trees, saying, "When the time comes, materials for watchtowers and palisades need not come from the people."
translations.idiomatic: He planted tens of thousands of mixed trees, saying, "When the time comes, materials for watchtowers and palisades need not come from the people."

sentences.zh: 人愛之，為立生祠。

translations.literal: The people loved him and erected a living shrine to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people loved him and erected a living shrine to him.

sentences.zh: 改武勝軍，又換鎮安軍節度使。

translations.literal: He was changed to Wusheng Circuit and then transferred to military commissioner of Zhen'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Wusheng Circuit, then to military commissioner of Zhen'an Circuit.

sentences.zh: 上書曰：「臣雖老，尚能為國守邊。」

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying, "Your servant, though old, can still guard the border for the state."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Though I am old, I can still guard the border for the state."

sentences.zh: 未報，得疾卒。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, he fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before a reply came, he fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 贈中書令，諡文簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted chief minister of the Secretariat and given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made chief minister of the Secretariat and given the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 琳為人敏厲深嚴，長於政事，辨議一出，不肯下人。

translations.literal: Lin was sharp, forceful, and deeply stern; he excelled in state affairs, and once he spoke in debate he would not yield to others.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was sharp, forceful, and deeply stern; he excelled in state affairs, and once he spoke in debate he would not yield to others.

sentences.zh: 然性嗇於財，而厚自奉養。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was stingy with wealth while lavish in his own upkeep.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by nature he was stingy with wealth while lavish in his own upkeep.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后時，嘗上《武后臨朝圖》，人以此薄之。

translations.literal: During Empress Dowager Zhangxian's regency, he once submitted the Illustration of Empress Wu Holding Court; people looked down on him for this.
translations.idiomatic: During Empress Dowager Zhangxian's regency, he once submitted the Illustration of Empress Wu Holding Court; people looked down on him for this.

sentences.zh: 姜遵，字從式，淄州長山人。

translations.literal: Jiang Zun, courtesy name Congshi, was a native of Changshan in Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zun, styled Congshi, came from Changshan in Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，為蓬萊尉，就辟登州司理參軍，開封府右軍巡判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as assistant magistrate of Penglai, then was recruited as judicial administrator of Dengzhou and right military patrol judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi, he served as assistant magistrate of Penglai, then was recruited as judicial administrator of Dengzhou and right military patrol judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 有疑獄，將抵死，遵辨出之。

translations.literal: In a doubtful criminal case where the accused was about to be executed, Zun argued and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: In a doubtful criminal case where the accused was about to be executed, Zun argued and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，王曾薦為監察御史，殿中侍御史，開封府判官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Wang Zeng recommended him as supervising censor, palace attendant censor, and judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Wang Zeng recommended him as supervising censor, palace attendant censor, and judicial officer of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 知吉州高惠連與遵有隙，發遵在廬陵時贓事，按驗無狀，猶降通判延州。

translations.literal: Gao Huilian, prefect of Jizhou, bore a grudge against Zun and exposed corruption from Zun's time in Luling; investigation found no substance, yet Zun was still demoted to vice-prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huilian, prefect of Jizhou, bore a grudge against Zun and exposed corruption from Zun's time in Luling; investigation found no substance, yet Zun was still demoted to vice-prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復入為侍御史、判戶部勾院。

translations.literal: He again entered the capital as attendant censor and was assigned to the Ministry of Revenue's audit office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as attendant censor and was put in charge of the Ministry of Revenue's audit office.

sentences.zh: 利州路饑，以遵為體量安撫，遷知邢州。

translations.literal: Lizhou Circuit suffered famine; Zun was appointed investigation-and-relief commissioner, then transferred to serve as prefect of Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Lizhou Circuit was stricken by famine, the court appointed Zun as investigation-and-relief commissioner, then transferred him to serve as prefect of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，徙滑州，為京東轉運使，徙京西。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, [Zun] was transferred to Huazhou, made Eastern Capital transport commissioner, then transferred to the Western Capital [circuit].
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong acceded, Zun was posted to Huazhou, made Eastern Capital transport commissioner, and then transferred to the Western Capital circuit.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以刑部郎中兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made vice director of the Ministry of Justice while concurrently serving as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Ministry of Justice while also serving as attendant censor in charge of miscellaneous business.

sentences.zh: 建言三司、開封府日接賓客，廢事，有詔禁止。

translations.literal: He proposed that the Three Fiscal Departments and Kaifeng Prefecture daily received guests and neglected their duties; an edict was issued forbidding this.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that the Three Fiscal Departments and Kaifeng Prefecture spent their days entertaining guests and neglecting official business, and an edict was issued to forbid the practice.

sentences.zh: 歷三司副使，再遷右諫議大夫、知永興軍。

translations.literal: He served as deputy commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments, then was promoted again to Right Remonstrance Counselor and military prefect of Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as deputy commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments, he was promoted again to Right Remonstrance Counselor and military prefect of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 奏罷咸陽富民元氏歲貢梨。

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish the annual tribute of pears from the wealthy Yuan clan of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish the annual pear tribute levied on the wealthy Yuan clan of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 召拜樞密副使，遷給事中，卒。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, promoted to Supervising Secretary, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, promoted to Supervising Secretary, and then died.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously awarded the title of Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 遵長於吏事，為治尚嚴猛，所誅殘者甚眾。

translations.literal: Zun excelled at administrative affairs; his governance favored severity and harshness, and those he had executed were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Zun was skilled in administrative work and governed with a stern, harsh hand; very many people were put to death under his rule.

sentences.zh: 在永興，太后嘗詔營浮屠，遵毀漢、唐碑碣代磚甓，既成，得召用。

translations.literal: While at Yongxing, the Empress Dowager once ordered a Buddhist pagoda built; Zun demolished Han and Tang steles to use as bricks and tiles. Once it was completed, he received a summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: While serving at Yongxing, the Empress Dowager once ordered a Buddhist pagoda built; Zun tore down Han and Tang steles to serve as bricks and tiles. When the work was finished, he received a summons back to office.

sentences.zh: 范雍，字伯純，世家太原。

translations.literal: Fan Yong, courtesy name Bochun, came from a distinguished family of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yong, styled Bochun, came from a distinguished family of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 曾祖仁恕，仕蜀為宰相。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Renshu served in Shu as grand councilor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Renshu had served in Shu as grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 祖從龜，刑部侍郎，入朝，改右屯衛將軍，後葬河南，遂為河南人。

translations.literal: His grandfather Conggui was Vice Minister of Justice; after entering the court he was changed to General of the Right Garrison Guard; later buried in Henan, and thus [the family] became Henan people.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Conggui had been Vice Minister of Justice; after entering the Song court he was reassigned as General of the Right Garrison Guard. He was later buried in Henan, and the family thus became Henan natives.

sentences.zh: 雍中進士第，為洛陽縣主簿。

translations.literal: Yong passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Luoyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Yong passed the jinshi examination and served as chief clerk of Luoyang County.

sentences.zh: 累官殿中丞、知端州。

translations.literal: He rose through posts to palace director and prefect of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to palace director and prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 寇準辟為河南通判，還，判三司開拆司。

translations.literal: Kou Zhun recruited him as vice-prefect of Henan; on return [to the capital] he was assigned to the Three Fiscal Departments' unpacking and inspection office.
translations.idiomatic: Kou Zhun recruited him as vice-prefect of Henan; on returning to the capital he was assigned to the Three Fiscal Departments' unpacking and inspection office.

sentences.zh: 河決滑州，選為京東轉運副使。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River burst its banks at Huazhou, he was selected as deputy Eastern Capital transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River broke its banks at Huazhou, he was selected as deputy Eastern Capital transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷河北、陝西轉運使，入為三司戶部副使，又徙度支。

translations.literal: He served successively as transport commissioner of Hebei and Shaanxi, entered [the capital] as deputy commissioner of the Households Bureau of the Three Fiscal Departments, then was transferred to the Expenditure Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as transport commissioner of Hebei and Shaanxi, then entered the capital as deputy commissioner of the Households Bureau of the Three Fiscal Departments before being transferred to the Expenditure Bureau.

sentences.zh: 以尚書工部郎中為龍圖閣待制、陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: As vice director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat, he became a Hanlin associate at the Dragon Diagram Hall and chief Shaanxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As vice director of the Ministry of Works in the Secretariat, he was made a Hanlin associate at the Dragon Diagram Hall and chief Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 還，提舉諸司庫務，勾當三班院。

translations.literal: On return [to the capital], he supervised the various treasury offices and managed affairs at the Three Ranks Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, he supervised the various treasury offices and managed affairs at the Three Ranks Bureau.

sentences.zh: 環、原州屬羌擾邊，以雍為安撫使。

translations.literal: When subordinate Qiang of Huan and Yuan prefectures troubled the border, Yong was made pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When subordinate Qiang tribes in Huan and Yuan prefectures harassed the frontier, Yong was appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建言：「屬羌因罪罰羊者，舊輸錢，而比年責使出羊，羌人頗以為患。

translations.literal: He proposed: "Among subordinate Qiang punished for offenses with the sheep penalty, they formerly paid money, but in recent years they have been compelled to furnish sheep, and the Qiang find this quite burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed: "Among the subordinate Qiang punished for offenses with the sheep penalty, they used to pay money, but in recent years they have been forced to supply sheep instead, and the Qiang find this quite burdensome.

sentences.zh: 請輸錢如舊，罪輕者以漢法贖金。」

translations.literal: Please let them pay money as before; for lighter offenses let them pay redemption money under Han law."
translations.idiomatic: Let them pay money as before, and for lighter offenses let them pay redemption fines under Han law."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、權三司使。

translations.literal: Promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor and acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Remonstrance Counselor and acting commissioner of the Three Fiscal Departments.

sentences.zh: 雍在京東時，平滑州水患。

translations.literal: While Yong was in the Eastern Capital [circuit], he smoothed away Huazhou's flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: While Yong was serving in the Eastern Capital circuit, he remedied the flood disaster at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 以勞加龍圖閣直學士。

translations.literal: For his labors he was additionally granted Dragon Diagram Hall academician.
translations.idiomatic: In recognition of his labors he was additionally granted the title of Dragon Diagram Hall academician.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，起復，遷給事中。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning, and promoted to Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After entering mourning for his mother, he was recalled from mourning and promoted to Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 玉清昭應宮災，章獻太后泣對大臣曰：「先帝竭力成此宮，一夕延燎幾盡，惟一二小殿存爾。」

translations.literal: When the Jade Hall of Clear Resplendence burned, Empress Dowager Zhangxian wept before the ministers and said, "The late emperor exhausted his strength to complete this palace; in one night the fire spread and nearly consumed it all, and only one or two small halls remain."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jade Hall of Clear Resplendence burned, Empress Dowager Zhangxian wept before the ministers and said, "The late emperor exhausted himself to build this palace; in a single night the fire spread and nearly destroyed it all, and only one or two small halls remain."

sentences.zh: 雍抗言曰：「不若悉燔之也。

translations.literal: Yong spoke up forcefully and said, "It would be better to burn it all down.
translations.idiomatic: Yong spoke up boldly and said, "It would be better to burn the whole thing down.

sentences.zh: 先朝以此竭天下之力，遽為灰燼，非出人意；

translations.literal: The previous reign exhausted the empire's strength on this, and it suddenly became ashes—this was beyond anyone's expectation;
translations.idiomatic: The previous reign exhausted the empire's strength on this, and it suddenly became ashes—no one could have foreseen it;

sentences.zh: 如因其所存，又將葺之，則民不堪命，非所以畏天戒也。」

translations.literal: if because something still stands we repair it again, the people cannot bear the burden, and this is not the way to revere Heaven's warning."
translations.idiomatic: but if we preserve what remains and rebuild it, the people will not be able to bear the burden, and that is not how we should heed Heaven's warning."

sentences.zh: 時王曾亦止之，遂詔勿葺。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Zeng also stopped it, and an edict was issued not to repair [the palace].
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng also argued against rebuilding at the time, and an edict was issued forbidding repairs.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太后崩，罷為戶部侍郎、知陝州，改永興軍。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager died, he was removed and made Vice Minister of Revenue and prefect of Shanzhou, then changed to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: After the Empress Dowager died, he was removed from office and made Vice Minister of Revenue and prefect of Shanzhou, then reassigned to Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 是歲饑疫，關中為甚，雍為振恤。

translations.literal: That year famine and pestilence struck, worst in Guanzhong; Yong provided relief.
translations.idiomatic: That year famine and pestilence struck, with Guanzhong hit hardest; Yong organized relief efforts.

sentences.zh: 以疾，請近郡，遂知河陽。

translations.literal: Due to illness he requested a nearby prefecture and was made prefect of Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: Because of illness he requested a nearby prefecture and was made prefect of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 進吏部侍郎，徙應天府，又改河南府，進資政殿學士。
