translations.literal: Mian said: "Striking when they are in peril and attacking during mourning is not the way of the Central Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "Striking when they are in peril and attacking during mourning is not the way of the Central Kingdom."

sentences.zh: 三司所給特支，物惡而估高，軍士有語，優人因戲及之。

translations.literal: The special disbursements given by the Three Departments — goods were poor but appraised high; soldiers murmured; entertainers in a play touched on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The special disbursements issued by the Three Departments were of poor quality but appraised at high value; soldiers complained, and entertainers in a play touched on the matter.

sentences.zh: 沔曰：「此朝廷特賜，何敢妄言動眾！」

translations.literal: Mian said: "This is a special grant from the court — how dare you rashly speak and stir up the masses!"
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "This is a special grant from the court — how dare you rashly speak and stir up the troops!"

sentences.zh: 命斬之徇。

translations.literal: He ordered the man beheaded as a public example.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the man beheaded as a public example.

sentences.zh: 將佐爭言：「此特戲爾，不足深罪也。」

translations.literal: Staff officers protested: "This was merely a jest — not a crime deserving deep punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Staff officers protested, "This was merely a jest — not a crime deserving severe punishment."

sentences.zh: 沔徐呼還，杖脊配嶺南，謂之曰：「汝賴戲我前，即私議動眾，汝必死，而告者超遷矣。」

translations.literal: Mian slowly called him back, flogged him and sentenced him to exile in Lingnan, telling him: "If you rely on jesting before me, you will privately discuss and stir up the masses; you would surely die, but the informer would be super-promoted."
translations.idiomatic: Mian slowly called him back, had him flogged and sentenced to exile in Lingnan, and told him, "If you rely on jesting before me, you will privately discuss and stir up the masses; you would surely die, but the informer would be super-promoted."

sentences.zh: 明日，給特支，士無敢歡者。

translations.literal: The next day when special disbursements were given, no soldier dared complain.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when special disbursements were issued, no soldier dared complain.

sentences.zh: 歷知陝州、河東都轉運使，又知慶州，聚戰亡遺骸葬祭之，軍中感泣。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Shaan Prefecture and Hedong grand transport commissioner; again as prefect of Qing, he gathered remains of the battle dead for burial and sacrifice; the army was moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Shaan Prefecture and Hedong grand transport commissioner; when he again governed Qing Prefecture, he gathered the remains of the battle dead for burial and sacrifice, and the army was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 凡三知慶州，邊人服其能。

translations.literal: Three times in all he governed Qing Prefecture; frontier people respected his competence.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Qing Prefecture three times in all, and the frontier people respected his competence.

sentences.zh: 遷龍圖閣直學士，又遷樞密直學士、知成都府，未至，以母喪罷。

translations.literal: Promoted to Dragon Hall academician; further promoted to Privy Council academician and prefect of Chengdu; before arriving, he was stopped on his mother's death.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Dragon Hall academician and further promoted to Privy Council academician and prefect of Chengdu, but before he arrived, he was stopped by his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服除，為陝西都轉運使。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he was made Shaanxi grand transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he was made Shaanxi grand transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 求知明州，會京東多盜，乃以知徐州，明購賞，嚴誅罰，盜遂止。

translations.literal: He requested Ming Prefecture; as eastern capital circuit had many bandits, he was instead made prefect of Xu Prefecture; he posted clear rewards and enforced severe punishments, and banditry ceased.
translations.idiomatic: He requested Ming Prefecture, but as the eastern capital circuit had many bandits, he was instead made prefect of Xu Prefecture; he posted clear rewards and enforced severe punishments, and banditry ceased.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州，時儂智高反，沔入見，帝以秦事勉之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qin Prefecture; when Nong Zhigao rebelled, Mian entered audience; the Emperor encouraged him regarding Qin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Qin Prefecture; when Nong Zhigao rebelled, Mian entered audience, and the Emperor encouraged him regarding affairs in Qin.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣雖老，然秦州不足煩聖慮，陛下當以嶺南為憂也。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant is old, but Qin Prefecture is not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern; Your Majesty ought to worry about the Lingnan region.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Your servant is old, but Qin Prefecture is not worth troubling Your Majesty's concern; Your Majesty ought to worry about the Lingnan region.

sentences.zh: 臣睹賊勢方張，官軍朝夕當有敗奏。」

translations.literal: I see the rebels' momentum is rising; government troops will soon send reports of defeat."
translations.idiomatic: I see the rebels' momentum is rising; government troops will soon be sending reports of defeat."

sentences.zh: 明日，聞蔣偕死，帝諭執政曰：「南事誠如沔所料。」

translations.literal: The next day, news came of Jiang Xie's death; the Emperor told the administration: "Southern affairs are indeed as Mian predicted."
translations.idiomatic: The next day, news came of Jiang Xie's death; the Emperor told the chief ministers, "Southern affairs are indeed as Mian predicted."

sentences.zh: 宰相龐籍奏遣沔行，以為湖南、江西路安撫使，以便宜從事，加廣南東、西路安撫使。

translations.literal: Chancellor Pang Ji memorialized to dispatch Mian; he was made Pacification Commissioner for Hunan and Jiangxi circuits with discretionary authority, and additionally made Pacification Commissioner for the Eastern and Western Guangnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Pang Ji memorialized to dispatch Mian; he was made Pacification Commissioner for Hunan and Jiangxi circuits with discretionary authority, and additionally made Pacification Commissioner for the Eastern and Western Guangnan circuits.

sentences.zh: 沔請益發騎兵，且增選偏裨二十八人，求武庫精甲五千。

translations.literal: Mian requested additional cavalry, moreover to select twenty-eight additional junior commanders, and sought five thousand sets of fine armor from the armory.
translations.idiomatic: Mian requested additional cavalry, the selection of twenty-eight additional junior commanders, and five thousand sets of fine armor from the armory.

sentences.zh: 參知政事梁適折之曰：「毋張皇！」

translations.literal: Co-administrator Liang Shi countered: "Do not alarm people!"
translations.idiomatic: Co-administrator Liang Shi countered, "Do not alarm people!"

sentences.zh: 沔曰：「前日惟亡備，故至此。

translations.literal: Mian said: "Previously we had no preparation — that is how we came to this.
translations.idiomatic: Mian said, "Previously we had no preparation — that is how we came to this.

sentences.zh: 今指期滅賊，非可以僥幸勝，乃欲示鎮靜耶？

translations.literal: Now to set a deadline for destroying the rebels — victory cannot be won by luck alone; or do you wish merely to show calm?
translations.idiomatic: Now, to set a deadline for destroying the rebels — victory cannot be won by luck alone; or do you wish merely to show calm?

sentences.zh: 夫實備不至而貌為鎮靜，危亡之道也。」

translations.literal: If actual preparedness is not achieved yet outward calm is shown — that is the path to peril and ruin."
translations.idiomatic: If actual preparedness is not achieved yet outward calm is shown, that is the path to peril and ruin."

sentences.zh: 居二日，促行，才與兵七百。

translations.literal: Two days later he was urged to depart; he was given only seven hundred troops.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later he was urged to depart, but he was given only seven hundred troops.

sentences.zh: 沔憂賊度嶺而北，乃檄湖南、北曰：「大兵且至，其繕治營壘，多具宴犒。」

translations.literal: Mian feared the rebels would cross the mountains northward; he therefore sent dispatches to Hunan and Hubei saying: "A great army is about to arrive — repair your camps and prepare abundant feasts and rewards."
translations.idiomatic: Mian feared the rebels would cross the mountains northward; he therefore sent dispatches to Hunan and Hubei saying, "A great army is about to arrive — repair your camps and prepare abundant feasts and rewards."

sentences.zh: 賊疑不敢北侵。

translations.literal: The rebels suspected a trap and did not dare invade north.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected a trap and did not dare invade north.

sentences.zh: 會遣狄青為宣撫使，沔與青會。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Di Qing was dispatched as pacification commissioner; Mian joined with Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Di Qing was dispatched as pacification commissioner, and Mian joined forces with him.

sentences.zh: 青與智高遇，戰歸仁鋪，智高敗走。

translations.literal: Qing met Zhigao in battle at Guiren Post; Zhigao was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qing met Zhigao in battle at Guiren Post; Zhigao was defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 青還，沔留治後事，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Qing returned; Mian remained to handle aftermath and was promoted to drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Qing returned; Mian remained to handle the aftermath and was promoted to drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 及還，帝問勞，解御帶賜之，以知杭州。

translations.literal: On his return, the Emperor inquired after him with commendation, removed his own belt and bestowed it, and made him prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On his return, the Emperor inquired after him with commendation, removed his own belt and bestowed it on him, and made him prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至南京，召為樞密副使。

translations.literal: Reaching Nanjing, he was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Nanjing, he was summoned as Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 張貴妃薨，追冊為皇后，命沔讀冊。

translations.literal: When Noble Consort Zhang died, she was posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and Mian was ordered to read the investiture text.
translations.idiomatic: When Noble Consort Zhang died, she was posthumously enfeoffed as empress, and Mian was ordered to read the investiture text.

sentences.zh: 故事，正后，翰林學士讀冊。

translations.literal: By precedent, for a legitimate empress a Hanlin academician reads the investiture text.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, for a legitimate empress a Hanlin academician reads the investiture text.

sentences.zh: 沔既陳不可用宰相護葬，且曰：「陛下若以臣沔讀冊則可，以樞密副使讀冊則不可。」

translations.literal: Mian had already stated that a chancellor could not be employed to escort the burial, and he said: "Your Majesty, if you have your servant Mian read the investiture text, that is acceptable; to have the vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs read it is not acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: Mian had already stated that a chancellor could not be employed to escort the burial, and he said, "Your Majesty, if you have me, Mian, read the investiture text, that is acceptable; to have the vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs read it is not acceptable."

sentences.zh: 遂求罷職。

translations.literal: He then requested dismissal from office.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 以資政殿學士知杭州。

translations.literal: He was made academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷大學士，徙知青州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand Academician and transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand academician and transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遷觀文殿學士、知幷州。

translations.literal: He was again transferred as academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred as academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 而諫官吳及、御史沈起奏沔淫縱無檢，守杭及幷所為不法，乃徙壽州。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials Wu Ji and investigating censor Shen Qi memorialized that Mian was profligate and unrestrained, and that his conduct while governing Hangzhou and Bingzhou was unlawful. He was therefore transferred to Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials Wu Ji and investigating censor Shen Qi memorialized that Mian was profligate and unrestrained and that his conduct while governing Hangzhou and Bingzhou was unlawful. He was therefore transferred to Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔按其跡，而使者奏：「沔在處州時，於遊人中見白牡丹者，遂誘與奸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered investigation of his conduct; the envoy reported: "When Mian was in Chuzhou, among travelers he saw one called White Peony and seduced her into illicit relations.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered an investigation of his conduct; the envoy reported, "When Mian was in Chuzhou, among travelers he saw a woman called White Peony and seduced her into illicit relations.

sentences.zh: 及在杭州，嘗從蕭山民鄭旻市紗，旻高其直，沔為恨。

translations.literal: In Hangzhou, he once bought gauze from the Xiangshan commoner Zheng Min; Min raised the price; Mian bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: In Hangzhou, he once bought gauze from the Xiangshan commoner Zheng Min; Min raised the price, and Mian bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 會旻貿紗有隱而不稅者，事覺，沔取其家簿記，積計不稅者幾萬端，配隸旻他州。

translations.literal: When Min's gauze trade had undeclared and untaxed portions exposed, Mian took his household records; accumulated untaxed goods totaled nearly ten thousand bolts, and Min was sentenced to penal service in another prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Min's gauze trade was found to include undeclared and untaxed goods, Mian seized his household records; the accumulated untaxed goods totaled nearly ten thousand bolts, and Min was sentenced to penal service in another prefecture.

sentences.zh: 州人許明有大珠百，沔妻弟邊珣以錢三萬三千強市之。

translations.literal: A native of the prefecture, Xu Ming, had a hundred large pearls; Mian's wife's younger brother Bian Xun forcibly purchased them for thirty-three thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: A native of the prefecture, Xu Ming, owned a hundred large pearls; Mian's wife's younger brother Bian Xun forcibly purchased them for thirty-three thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 沔愛明所藏郭虔暉畫《鷹圖》，明不以獻。

translations.literal: Mian admired Ming's treasured painting Eagle by Guo Qianhui; Ming would not present it.
translations.idiomatic: Mian admired Ming's treasured painting Eagle by Guo Qianhui, but Ming would not give it to him.

sentences.zh: 初，明父禱水仙大王廟生明，故幼名「大王兒」。

translations.literal: Initially, Ming's father prayed at the Water Immortal King shrine for a son and Ming was born; hence his childhood name King's Son.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, Ming's father had prayed at the Water Immortal King shrine for a son, and Ming was born; hence his childhood name King's Son.

sentences.zh: 沔即捕按明僭稱王，取其畫鷹，刺配之。

translations.literal: Mian immediately arrested Ming on the charge of presumptuously calling himself king, seized his Eagle painting, and sentenced him to tattooed exile.
translations.idiomatic: Mian immediately arrested Ming on the charge of presumptuously calling himself king, seized his Eagle painting, and sentenced him to tattooed exile.

sentences.zh: 及沔罷去，明詣提點刑獄，斷一臂自訟，乃得釋。

translations.literal: When Mian was dismissed and left, Ming went to the judicial intendant, severed an arm to plead his own case, and was finally released.
translations.idiomatic: When Mian was dismissed and left office, Ming went to the judicial intendant, severed an arm to plead his own case, and was finally released.

sentences.zh: 杭州人金氏女，沔白晝使吏卒輿致，亂之。

translations.literal: A Hangzhou woman surnamed Jin — Mian in broad daylight sent clerks and soldiers to carry her off by sedan and violated her.
translations.idiomatic: A Hangzhou woman surnamed Jin — Mian in broad daylight sent clerks and soldiers to carry her off by sedan and violated her.

sentences.zh: 有趙氏女已許嫁莘旦，沔見西湖上，遂設計取趙女至州宅，與飲食臥起。

translations.literal: A woman surnamed Zhao had been promised in marriage to Shen Dan; Mian saw her on West Lake and schemed to take Zhao to the prefectural residence, sharing meals and lodging with her.
translations.idiomatic: A woman surnamed Zhao had been promised in marriage to Shen Dan; Mian saw her on West Lake and schemed to take her to the prefectural residence, sharing meals and lodging with her.

sentences.zh: 所刺配人以百數，及罷，盜其按去，後有訴冤者多以無按，不能自解。

translations.literal: Those he sentenced to tattooed exile numbered in the hundreds; when dismissed, he stole the case files; afterward many who petitioned about injustice could not be released for lack of records.
translations.idiomatic: Those he sentenced to tattooed exile numbered in the hundreds; when he was dismissed, he stole the case files, and afterward many who petitioned about injustice could not be cleared for lack of records.

sentences.zh: 在幷州，私役使吏卒，往來青州、麟州市賣紗、絹、綿、紙、藥物。

translations.literal: In Bingzhou, he privately compelled clerks and soldiers to travel between Qing and Linzhou selling gauze, silk, cotton, paper, and medicines.
translations.idiomatic: In Bingzhou, he privately compelled clerks and soldiers to travel between Qing and Linzhou selling gauze, silk, cotton, paper, and medicines.

sentences.zh: 官庭列大梃，或以暴怒擊訴事者，嘗剔取盜足後筋，斷之。」

translations.literal: In the official hall he arrayed great cudgels; in fits of rage he sometimes beat those bringing lawsuits; once he stripped a thief's Achilles tendon and severed it."
translations.idiomatic: In the official hall he arrayed great cudgels; in fits of rage he sometimes beat those bringing lawsuits, and once he stripped a thief's Achilles tendon and severed it."

sentences.zh: 奏至，乃責寧國節度副使，監司坐失察，皆被絀。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Mian was demoted to vice military governor of Ningguo; supervisory officials were punished for failure to oversee — all received demerits.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Mian was demoted to vice military governor of Ningguo; supervisory officials were punished for failure to oversee, and all received demerits.

sentences.zh: 其後復光祿卿，分司南京，居宿州。

translations.literal: Afterward he was restored as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, honorary appointee at Nanjing, residing in Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was restored as Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, honorary appointee at Nanjing, and resided in Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 會恩，知濠州，以尚書禮部侍郎致仕。

translations.literal: On a grace amnesty, he was made prefect of Hao; he retired as Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On a grace amnesty, he was made prefect of Hao and retired as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，遷戶部。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was promoted to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong acceded, he was promoted to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝與執政議守邊者，難其人，參知政事歐陽修奏：「孫沔向守環慶，養練士卒，招撫蕃夷，恩信最著。

translations.literal: The emperor discussed with the chief ministers who should guard the border, but found no suitable candidate; participation in state affairs Ouyang Xiu submitted a memorial saying, "Sun Mian formerly guarded Huan and Qing, trained and drilled troops, and won over the frontier tribes—his kindness and trustworthiness were most outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor discussed border defense with his chief ministers but could find no suitable candidate; councilor Ouyang Xiu memorialized: "Sun Mian once held Huan and Qing, trained troops, and won over frontier tribes—none was more trusted.

sentences.zh: 今雖七十，心力不衰，中間曾以罪廢，然宜棄瑕使過。」

translations.literal: Though he is now seventy, his mind and strength have not declined; he was once dismissed for an offense in the interim, yet his faults should be set aside and his past service employed."
translations.idiomatic: Though he is seventy, his mind and strength have not declined; he was once dismissed for an offense, yet his faults should be set aside and his past service employed."

sentences.zh: 遂起為資政殿學士、知河中府，又以為觀文殿學士、知慶州，徙延州，道卒。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was recalled as academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and appointed prefect of Hezhong, then made academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Qingzhou, transferred to Yanzhou, and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as academician of the Hall for Cultivating Governance and made prefect of Hezhong, then academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Qingzhou, transferred to Yanzhou, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 沔居官以才力聞，強直少所憚，然喜宴遊女色，故中間坐廢。

translations.literal: Mian was known in office for his talent and energy; he was forceful and straightforward and feared little, yet he delighted in feasting, travel, and women, and so was dismissed in the interim.
translations.idiomatic: Mian was known in office for talent and energy; he was forceful and straightforward and feared little, yet he delighted in feasting, travel, and women, and so was dismissed midway through his career.

sentences.zh: 妻邊氏悍妒，為一時所傳。

translations.literal: His wife, Lady Bian, was fierce and jealous—a story widely told in her day.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Bian, was fierce and jealous—a story widely told in her day.

sentences.zh: 初，陝西用兵，朝廷多假邊帥倚以集事，近臣出帥或驕恣越法。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shaanxi was at war, the court often relied on frontier commanders to gather affairs, and close ministers sent out as commanders sometimes grew arrogant and overstepped the law.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Shaanxi campaigns, the court often relied on frontier commanders to get things done, and close ministers sent out as commanders sometimes grew arrogant and overstepped the law.

sentences.zh: 及沔廢後，真定路安撫使呂溱繼得罪，自此守帥之權宜微矣。

translations.literal: After Mian was dismissed, Zhending Circuit pacification commissioner Lü Zhen likewise fell afoul of the law; from then on the authority of frontier commanders was appropriately reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After Mian was dismissed, Zhending Circuit pacification commissioner Lü Zhen likewise fell afoul of the law; from then on frontier commanders held appropriately less power.

sentences.zh: 論曰：君子惟能立身，而後可以佐國。

translations.literal: The commentator says: a gentleman must first be able to establish himself before he can assist the state.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: a gentleman must first establish himself before he can serve the state.

sentences.zh: 中正、起自陷朋黨，遵、稹憸邪，沔頗知兵而以汙敗。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng and Qi brought themselves down through factional entanglement; Zun and Zhen were crafty and corrupt; Mian was quite knowledgeable in military affairs yet ruined by misconduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng and Qi fell through factional entanglement; Zun and Zhen were crafty and corrupt; Mian knew warfare well yet was ruined by misconduct.

sentences.zh: 琳有才器，能斷大事，然獻《武后臨朝圖》於章獻，君子鄙之。

translations.literal: Lin had talent and capacity and could decide great affairs, yet he presented the Illustration of Empress Wu Holding Court to Empress Dowager Zhangxian—men of principle despised him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had talent and could decide great affairs, yet he presented the Illustration of Empress Wu Holding Court to Empress Dowager Zhangxian—men of principle despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 雍任邊寄而覆軍敗將，幾不自保。

translations.literal: Yong was entrusted with the frontier yet lost armies and defeated generals, and nearly could not save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was entrusted with the frontier yet lost armies and defeated generals, and nearly could not save himself.

sentences.zh: 若訥喜申、韓、管子之書，中師、布少所建明，殆亦未足與議也。

translations.literal: Ruone delighted in the books of Shenzi, Han Feizi, and Master Guan; Zhongshi and Bu accomplished little of note—they were scarcely worth discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Ruone delighted in the books of Shenzi, Han Feizi, and Master Guan; Zhongshi and Bu accomplished little of note—they were scarcely worth discussing.
